components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The June 23 tech-led rout (S&P -1.4%, Nasdaq sharply lower, semis crushed as Korea's KOSPI fell ~double-digits) knocked the index back toward its 125-day average; momentum has flipped from the one bullish component to neutral-to-soft.

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. With the semiconductor complex leading a sharp drawdown, new lows are expanding again and the net-highs reading has weakened.

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). The brief mid-June broadening reversed on the June 23 tech selloff; declining volume is again outpacing advancing volume.

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options buyers turned defensive into the semis drawdown and the hawkish FOMC dot-plot, favoring puts.

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. Volatility popped on the June 23 tech rout but remains off the early-June war-scare highs — elevated but not panicked.

components.name: Safe Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Bonds have outperformed stocks over the trailing window as equities sold off, signaling defensive positioning.

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. Spreads remain historically tight (HY OAS near ~280bp) but the demand for risky credit has cooled with the equity wobble.

breadth.note: Breadth deteriorated late in the period: a record-flow, risk-on mid-June rally (huge equity-fund inflows in the week to June 17) gave way to a sharp June 23 semiconductor-led drawdown (Technology -~4%, KOSPI -~10%) after a hawkish FOMC dot-plot and a BofA rate-hike warning. The McClellan Oscillator/Summation Index and cumulative A-D line never durably reversed their multi-week downtrend, so the tape remains internally narrow with index strength still propped up by a handful of mega-caps rather than broad participation.

flows.period: Week ended June 17, 2026 (reported June 19, 2026); weekly/lagged. NOTE: this record risk-on week PREDATES the June 23 tech/semiconductor selloff, so it captures the post-Iran-deal 'buy-the-dip' surge, not the late-week reversal.
flows.narrative: A violent risk-on reversal. After the prior week's US-led outflows, LSEG Lipper data showed a net ~$55.2B poured into global equity funds in the week to June 17 — the strongest weekly inflow since November 2024 — as the June 15 US-Iran framework deal collapsed the war premium and investors aggressively bought the dip. Technology funds drew a record ~$21.5B (largest weekly tech allocation ever), Europe took ~$10.7B and Asia ~$3.9B, while industrials added ~$2.5B. Emerging-market equity funds were the lone holdout, bleeding ~$2.9B for an eighth straight weekly outflow as a hawkish-leaning Fed and firm dollar weighed. The flows are weekly and lagged, and the subsequent June 23 semiconductor-led rout suggests this euphoric tech allocation was poorly timed.
